hook.text: A false claim about vaccines reached 100 million people before fact-checkers even noticed it existed.

buildup.text: MIT found falsehoods spread six times faster than truth on Twitter. Lies are novel; truth is boring.

discovery.text: False news triggers surprise and disgust—high-arousal emotions that drive sharing. Truth triggers nothing.

twist.text: Corrections travel ten times slower than the original lie. By the time truth arrives, belief is set.

climax.text: The 'illusory truth effect' means repeated lies feel true. Viral repetition becomes belief.

punchline.text: A lie shared enough times becomes the truth.

quiz.question: Why does false news spread faster than truth?
